# Meal allowances, communal provisioning and a refused supplement

**Reading layers:** [Raw output · Edited output · Readable German · Conditional interpretation](../../docs/reading-conventions.md). In decoded streams, `?` marks one unresolved position; `X` and numeral/letter labels remain literal.

**Source:** J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
printed p129 B1, p133 A2–A3 and p134 A4; PDF pp132, 136 and 137.
**Edition:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

These four numbered parts form one message. The repeated receipt header
is `NKJ FUER COS v LP (7.18 a.m., November 6th)`, and the origin line is
`2400 (5/11) 4 TEILE`. The pages carry the heading 5 November 1918 and
explicit continuation annotations. The matching headers and numbers
provide the cross-page link despite the intervening pages of other
traffic.

The message disputes high cash meal allowances, requires rates to be
reduced, promotes communal purchasing and provision of food in kind,
and refuses an application for a cost-of-living supplement. It supplies
no actual allowance rate. The [experiment](../../experiments/military_allowances/README.md)
contains every source crop, coordinate and candidate edit.

## p129 B1

The source advertises and prints **398 slots**, including a dash in
`XVFX-` and an invalid `C` in `CFGVV`. Their raw 199-position reading is:

**Raw output:**

```text
?UXMXRMX30NRX228XFUERSELBSTVERPFLEGERDORTFESTGESETETEBEKOESTBGUNGSGELDERSINUZUHOCHUNDMUESSENAUCHFUERRUECKLIEGENDEZEITBEANSTANDETWERDENXSCHWEDISCHEGEVUE?RNISSEKOENNENNICHTALSSASSGEBENDANGESEHENWERDENX
```

The ordinary-word candidate is:

**Edited output:**

```text
ZUXMXRMX30NRX228XFUERSELBSTVERPFLEGERDORTFESTGESETZTEBEKOESTIGUNGSGELDERSINDZUHOCHUNDMUESSENAUCHFUERRUECKLIEGENDEZEITBEANSTANDETWERDENXSCHWEDISCHEGEBUEHRNISSEKOENNENNICHTALSMASSGEBENDANGESEHENWERDENX
```

It requires **five observed-coordinate substitutions and two printed
erasure fills**. The initial reference remains unexpanded. With
editorial spacing, the substantive passage reads:

**Readable German:**

> Für Selbstverpfleger dort festgesetzte Beköstigungsgelder sind zu hoch und müssen auch für rückliegende Zeit beanstandet werden. Schwedische Gebührnisse können nicht als maßgebend angesehen werden.

This does not identify any particular Swedish schedule or numerical rate.

## p133 A2

The source advertises and prints **452 slots**. The opening `VXDVV` group
is five characters, and the last group of the seventh row is the literal
`VAXGL`, with an invalid final `L`. The raw text is:

**Raw output:**

```text
HOHESELBSTBEKOESTIGUNGSGELDERBILDENDAUERNDERANREIZSICHDERALSREGELGEDACHTENNATURALVERPFLEGUNGZUENTZIEHENXHERABSETZ?NGDAHERDNBEDINGTERFORDERLICHXBEINEUFESTSETZUNGSINDDIEFUEREINEFELDKOSTPORTIONAUFZUWENDENDENPREISEZUGRUNDEZDLEGENX
```

The candidate costs **four observed-coordinate substitutions and one
printed-glyph fill**:

**Edited output:**

```text
HOHESELBSTBEKOESTIGUNGSGELDERBILDENDAUERNDENANREIZSICHDERALSREGELGEDACHTENNATURALVERPFLEGUNGZUENTZIEHENXHERABSETZUNGDAHERUNBEDINGTERFORDERLICHXBEINEUFESTSETZUNGSINDDIEFUEREINEFELDKOSTPORTIONAUFZUWENDENDENPREISEZUGRUNDEZULEGENX
```

With editorial spacing:

**Readable German:**

> Hohe Selbstbeköstigungsgelder bilden dauernden Anreiz, sich der als Regel gedachten Naturalverpflegung zu entziehen. Herabsetzung daher unbedingt erforderlich. Bei Neufestsetzung sind die für eine Feldkostportion aufzuwendenden Preise zugrunde zu legen.

`BEI NEUFESTSETZUNG` is already present in the source-aligned raw reading;
it is not an added editorial phrase.

## p133 A3

This part is advertised as **486 coordinates**, and the literal source
contains exactly 486. Earlier OCR made the first group `VAGAG` seven
slots and omitted the complete final `GXFVD A`, leaving an incorrect
482-slot stream. Correcting the transcription produces the following
**243-position direct reading**:

**Raw output:**

```text
NATURALVERPFLEGUNGMUSSREGELBILDENXDIESEDURCHGEMEINSAMENEINKAUFXUMPREISENICHTUNNOETIGINHOEHEZUTREIBENUNDDURCHEINRICHTUNGDEUTSCHERSPEISEHAEUSERNACHMOEGLICHKEITFOERDERNSODASSSELBSTVERPFLEGUNGAUFTATSAECHLICHNICHTZUUMGEHENDEFAELLEBESCHRAENKTBLEIBTX
```

Every plaintext pair is complete. **No source coordinate is changed or
filled.** The text encrypts back exactly to the observed source using
the unchanged Nov4–6 key.

With editorial spacing:

**Readable German:**

> Naturalverpflegung muss Regel bilden. Diese durch gemeinsamen Einkauf, um Preise nicht unnötig in Höhe zu treiben, und durch Einrichtung deutscher Speisehäuser nach Möglichkeit fördern, sodass Selbstverpflegung auf tatsächlich nicht zu umgehende Fälle beschränkt bleibt.

The passage calls for communal purchasing to avoid unnecessary price
increases and for German dining facilities to reduce reliance on cash
self-provisioning. It does not state that such facilities had already
been established.

## p134 A4

The source advertises and prints **424 valid coordinates**. Its raw
212-character text is:

**Raw output:**

```text
BALDIGEMITTEILUNGDESDORTSEITSVERANLASSTENERBETEN0BEANTRAGTETEUERUNGSZULAGEKANNNICHTGEWAEHRTWERDENXZULAGEREGELUNGMUSSNACHPASCHEXRMX2XVORSCHRIFTERFOLGENXKRIEGSMINISTERIUMARMEEVERWALTUNGSDEPARTEMENTXNRX1235X18XGXBX1
```

The candidate changes only the raw `0` after `ERBETEN` to `X`, costing
**one coordinate substitution**.

**Readable German — body excerpt; the closing reference is retained immediately below:**

> Baldige Mitteilung des dortseits Veranlassten erbeten. Beantragte Teuerungszulage kann nicht gewährt werden. Zulageregelung muss nach PASCHE X RM X 2 Vorschrift erfolgen. Kriegsministerium, Armeeverwaltungsdepartement …

The `PASCHE X RM X 2` wording and full closing
`NR X 1235 X 18 X G X B X 1` are retained as received. No unverified title,
author, edition or regulation is supplied for `PASCHE`. The `0→X` repair
does not imply a global relabeling of zero elsewhere.

## Attribution, counts and verification

The period key is previously published. Parts one, two and four also
predate this edition as readable unreviewed repository candidates.
Part three was unreadable under its earlier OCR frame; the old outputs
are frozen alongside the corrected source edition. The contribution
here is complete source assembly, recovery of that direct reading and
reversible candidate repairs. The bounded paper, dissertation and
comment-thread check does not establish historical decipherment priority.

The four records contain **1,760 printed source slots**, of which
**1,757** are valid ADFGVX coordinates. They yield **880 plaintext
positions**: 877 fixed in the raw models and all 880 in the explicit
candidates. Total cost is **10 observed substitutions and three printed
erasure fills**, with no key, rank or length changes. These counts describe
the edition's coverage, not the number of newly solved key symbols.

```bash
python experiments/military_allowances/verify.py --verify
python experiments/military_allowances/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

# Radio service: Eilvese repetition and a garbled Caucasus message

**Reading layers:** [Raw output · Edited output · Readable German · Conditional interpretation](../../docs/reading-conventions.md). In decoded streams, `?` marks one unresolved position; `X` and numeral/letter labels remain literal.

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p132 contains three separate records: a partly garbled request for
an officer-register extract, a conditional recovery of a repeat-transmission
instruction for Eilvese, and an exact request to repeat a garbled incoming
Caucasus message. The unchanged published `Nov4-6` key applies throughout.
The middle record is genuinely odd in length and requires a separate
before-transposition error model; the other two have ordinary exact frames.

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p132, PDF p135](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [full page](../../experiments/november_radio_service/sources/childs_p132_full.png)
is headed `5th NOVEMBER, 1918.`

## A: an officer-register request, with the name unresolved

The [A source](../../experiments/november_radio_service/sources/childs_p132_A.png)
has this header and exactly 242 slots, including one printed dash:

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) OSM v OUI (9.29 p.m., November 5th)
HIER 13 2207
RICHI-242
```

The raw 121-position reading fixes 120 positions:

**Raw output:**

```text
MILLTAEGMISZIONKOSJOIIXUEBERTENDUNGEILESKRIEGSRANGLI?TRNAUSZUGESDESGENERALMAJRHYDEWALDERBETENXFELDEISENBAHNNHEFPAFR53540X
```

Six observed-coordinate substitutions and one dash fill repair ordinary
words, giving:

**Edited output:**

```text
MILITAERMISZIONKOSJOIIXUEBERSENDUNGEINESKRIEGSRANGLISTENAUSZUGESDESGENERALMAJRHYDEWALDERBETENXFELDEISENBAHNCHEFPAFR53540X
```

The readable clause is:

**Readable German:**

> Übersendung eines Kriegsranglistenauszuges des `GENERALMAJRHYDEWALD`
> erbeten. Feldeisenbahnchef `PAFR53540`.

It requests an extract from a wartime officer register. **The addressee/place
field `KOSJOII` and the general-name field `GENERALMAJRHYDEWALD` remain
unresolved.** Neither is expanded into an identified person or place. The
raw `MISZION` spelling and `PAFR53540` footer also remain literal. This is a
partial source edition, not a securely identified personnel record.

## B: repeat the fourth-period telegram in the fifth

The [B source](../../experiments/november_radio_service/sources/childs_p132_B.png)
is marked with explicit urgency:

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) LP v NKJ (6.13 p.m., November 5th)
SSD EILT SOFORT LOESEN 1410 (5)
RIZI-155
```

The printed length and manual transcription both give **155 slots**. There
are two printed dashes in group `XFF--`; all other coordinates are retained.
The direct odd-frame reading has 77 paired positions and one unpaired coordinate:

**Raw output — original odd frame; paired prefix and orphan coordinate reported separately:**

```text
FFEREILVESEXWIEDERHOLETT?LEGGWD3?MYMFLWF7MFFS7KFNT8RLTIWFWUAFQLL3F1QF7PZNMDQQ
```

The latter portion becomes readable under the opposite coordinate-pair
phase. The following **conditional model** produces the cleanest short
telegram wording: one extra `V` was present in the fractionated intermediate
stream before its 155-slot column transposition.

After undoing that original transposition, interim indices **54, 55, 56 and
57** are four identical consecutive `V` coordinates. Removing any one of
them gives the same 154-coordinate stream and this conditional raw reading:

**Raw output — conditional deletion of one V at interim indices 54–57 after untransposition:**

```text
FFEREILVESEXWIEDERHOLETT?LEGRXVO?VIERTERPERIODEINFU1NFTERXGEBETSORHER5MINXVVV
```

Three observed-coordinate substitutions and two printed-dash fills give:

**Edited output — same conditional interim-deletion model, with the stated repairs and fills:**

```text
FUEREILVESEXWIEDERHOLETTELEGRXVONVIERTERPERIODEINFUENFTERXGEBETVORHER5MINXVVV
```

Readable German, expanding only the telegram abbreviation in brackets:

**Readable German:**

> Für Eilvese. Wiederholet Telegr[amm] von vierter Periode in fünfter.
> Gebet vorher 5 Min. VVV.

It asks Eilvese to repeat the fourth-period telegram during the fifth period
and send **five minutes of `VVV`** beforehand. The old imperative forms
`WIEDERHOLET` and `GEBET` are preserved. The paper by Lasry and colleagues
separately identifies Eilvese and its OUI callsign in its discussion of
p120/p123; that supplies station context, not prior publication of this p132
body. [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461, §6.5](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461)

### Exact costs and the four equivalent positions

| Received source index, zero-based | Printed group / position, one-based | Change | Effect |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 52 | 11 / 3 | `X` → `F` | `SORHER` → `VORHER` |
| 64 | 13 / 5 | `A` → `D` | `FFER` → `FUER` |
| 88 | 18 / 4 | `A` → `F` | `FU1NFTER` → `FUENFTER` |
| 103 | 21 / 4 | printed dash → `F` | Missing `E` in `TELEGR` |
| 104 | 21 / 5 | printed dash → `X` | Missing `N` in `VON` |

The raw numeral label `1` in `FU1NFTER` is retained in both raw readings.
Its change to `E` is an explicit local coordinate repair within a word; it
does not reassign the square's digit `1`. The numerical `5` in `5MIN` remains
unchanged.

The extra coordinate is separately charged as **one extraneous intermediate
coordinate**. It is not silently discarded from the received source. To
reproduce the 155-slot witness, encode the 77-character proposal, reinsert
the same `V` at the selected interim position, and apply the original rank
order. All four choices produce the same transmitted witness after the
five listed repairs/fills. Their differing source origins are retained in
the certificate; there is no uniquely identified extra `V`.

An initial insertion-only search retrieved the useful ending but left
`TELEGAR` or `TELERGR`. Those earlier candidates remain in the
[geometry audit](../../experiments/november_radio_service/geometry_audit.json).
The later extra-coordinate interpretation was selected after inspecting
the source and wording. All 156 one-insertion and 155 one-removal interim
positions are preserved. For this retrospective 77-character template,
the four identical-V removals uniquely form the minimum-cost set of three
substitutions and two dash fills. This is a conditional consistency result,
not independent proof of the historical mechanism.

## C: request to repeat a garbled incoming message

The [C source](../../experiments/november_radio_service/sources/childs_p132_C.png)
has this header:

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
C) NKJ v LP (7.45 p.m., November 6th)
FUER COS 2150 (5/11)
RICHI-198
```

The November 5 origin line and November 6 reception line are retained.
All 198 coordinates and all 99 plaintext labels are fixed without repair:

**Raw output:**

```text
KAUKASUSDELEGAXWIEDERHLGVERSTUEMMELTEINGEGXOSKACHIX54GRXSSX1912XANXNACHCHEFERBETENXNACHCHE5X150527X
```

The message addresses the Caucasus delegation and asks for repetition of a
garbled incoming message to `NACHCHEF`. Its literal reference is
`OSKACHI 54GR SS 1912`; the footer is `NACHCHE5 150527`. Those abbreviations
and numerical labels, including the final `5` in `NACHCHE5`, remain as read.
No new numbering interpretation or silent spelling change is introduced.

## Source status and reproducibility

The [inputs](../../experiments/november_radio_service/inputs.json) preserve
manual rows, literal headers, key provenance and source-image hashes. The
[certificate](../../experiments/november_radio_service/certificates.json)
records the raw and conditional readings, all possible label domains,
coordinate origins and exact forward witnesses. A remains partly garbled
at its names; B remains conditional on the extra-coordinate model; C is an
unchanged direct reading.

The period key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [2016, DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also reproduced in George Lasry's [2017-02-24 comment 4](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).
Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates existed. The bounded paper check
found no explicit p132 body example; no universal first-decipherment claim
is made.

```sh
python experiments/november_radio_service/verify.py --verify
python experiments/november_radio_service/geometry_audit.py --verify
```

# Naval inquiry: has the referenced SKL item arrived?

**Reading layers:** [Raw output · Edited output · Readable German · Conditional interpretation](../../docs/reading-conventions.md). In decoded streams, `?` marks one unresolved position; `X` and numeral/letter labels remain literal.

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

## p108 A

Childs p108 A, PDF p111, is headed
`OSM v LP (1.00 p.m., November 3rd)` and
`1900 (2/11) SONDERKOMMANDO IN DER TUERKEI`.
The [source crop](../../experiments/p108_naval_and_personnel/sources/p108_A.png)
contains **282 valid coordinates**, matching `RICHI-282`.
The unchanged published **Nov1–3** key gives a complete reading without
source-coordinate repairs.

**Raw output — native 282-coordinate frame:**

```text
SLX4314XAUFXGGX2890XEINSXFRAGEDOPPELPUNKTXISTXSKLXBNRXGGX546XROEMX3XNUNMEHRDORTHINGELANGTFRAGEZEICHENXADMIRALSTABSEEKRIEGSLTGXGX1121XROEMX3XX
```

**Edited output — unchanged, with zero substitutions or fills:**

```text
SLX4314XAUFXGGX2890XEINSXFRAGEDOPPELPUNKTXISTXSKLXBNRXGGX546XROEMX3XNUNMEHRDORTHINGELANGTFRAGEZEICHENXADMIRALSTABSEEKRIEGSLTGXGX1121XROEMX3XX
```

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation; DOPPELPUNKT and FRAGEZEICHEN are rendered as their punctuation marks:**

> SL. 4314. Auf GG. 2890. Eins. Frage: Ist SKL, BNr. GG. 546, Röm. 3,
> nunmehr dorthin gelangt? Admiralstab, Seekriegsltg. G. 1121. Röm. 3.

The message asks whether the item identified by **SKL BNR GG 546 ROEM 3**
has arrived. It does not report an arrival. Routing and reference
abbreviations remain unexpanded, and no numerical label is reassigned.

## Conditional interpretation and the OCR correction

The earlier corpus OCR retained only 280 coordinates, omitting the final
standalone **FX** row that is plainly visible at the bottom of the body.
It also masked source index **11**, the F in **GFGXV**. Recovering those
three visible glyphs from the scan restores the printed 282-coordinate
frame and all **141 / 141 fixed plaintext positions**. This is a correction
to the OCR transcript, not a conjectural insertion into the historical
source. The unchanged complete plaintext re-encrypts to the visible
ciphertext exactly.

The [frozen OCR snapshot](../../experiments/p108_naval_and_personnel/ocr_snapshot.json)
and [certificate](../../experiments/p108_naval_and_personnel/certificates.json)
retain the old 280-coordinate input, its output under the same key and
the exact source-visible difference. The old shared corpus is unchanged.
The neighboring personnel message has a different header and is treated
separately; adjacency alone is not used to join it to this inquiry.

The edition retains published key credit and the earlier unread OCR
candidate. Bounded prior-publication checks do not establish historical
priority, and no first-solution claim is made. See the
[inputs](../../experiments/p108_naval_and_personnel/inputs.json) and
[reproduction instructions](../../experiments/p108_naval_and_personnel/README.md).
headings: # Naval inquiry: has the referenced SKL item arrived?
## Conditional interpretation and the OCR correction
